data.description:
## Description

**What**: A user-manual story (no Claude autonomy possible) covering the human steps required to provision an OpenAI API key and switch this project's `.claude/dso-config.conf` to use OpenAI as the CI review provider.
**Why**: Phase 2's plumbing (P2-S1/P2-S2/P2-S3) makes provider switching possible; this story is the operational flip for THIS repository. Without it, OpenAI support exists in code but no CI run on this repo would actually exercise it. Tagged `manual:awaiting_user` because key provisioning and secret management require human action.
**Scope**:
- IN: User-side OpenAI key generation; GitHub Actions secret upload; live `.claude/dso-config.conf` edit to set `model.provider=openai` + tier IDs; user confirmation handshake; first-run CI verification PR
- OUT: Any code/script changes (those are P2-S1/P2-S2/P2-S3); reference config defaults (P2-S1 owns those); workflow file (P2-S3 owns ci.yml); any change to the local Anthropic-pinned namespace

## Done Definitions

- When this story is complete, the user has generated an OpenAI API key from platform.openai.com (or the appropriate organizational account) with sufficient quota/tier for deep-tier 4-call bursts on the configured deep model
  ← Satisfies: "OpenAI provider path produces schema-conformant output"
- When this story is complete, the user has added the key as the `OPENAI_API_KEY` secret in this repository's GitHub Actions secrets at the correct scope; presence is verified via `gh secret list` (the secret name appears in the list output) and recorded as a story comment
  ← Satisfies: "OpenAI provider path produces schema-conformant output"
- When this story is complete, `.claude/dso-config.conf` in this repository is updated to set `model.provider=openai`, `model.light=<verified-OpenAI-light-id>`, `model.standard=<verified-OpenAI-standard-id>`, `model.deep=<verified-OpenAI-deep-id>` — using the OpenAI model IDs verified against the live OpenAI model list during P2-S3 (not training-data assumptions); the change is committed via `/dso:commit` so the review gate sees the new config in the standard flow
  ← Satisfies: "OpenAI provider path produces schema-conformant output"
- When this story is complete, the user has acknowledged the provisioning step in a story comment (e.g., "OPENAI_API_KEY provisioned and project flipped to OpenAI provider"); this acknowledgement is the manual:awaiting_user handshake
  ← Satisfies: "OpenAI provider path produces schema-conformant output"
- When this story is complete, a subsequent PR opened against this repository (any small change suffices) successfully completes the CI `llm-review` job using the OpenAI provider — `reviewer-findings.json` is produced, passes the existing JSON schema with all 5 dimension scores populated, and the GitHub Actions log shows the review ran against `api.openai.com` rather than `api.anthropic.com`
  ← Satisfies: "OpenAI provider path produces schema-conformant output"

## Considerations

- [Security] The OpenAI API key is a long-lived credential — provision at the repo (or org) scope using GitHub Actions encrypted secrets, NOT committed to any file or pasted into chat
- [Reliability] OpenAI rate limits depend on account tier; if the deep tier (4-call burst on the flagship model) hits 429s on a Tier 1 account, escalate to upgrade the OpenAI tier or temporarily downgrade `model.deep` to a less rate-limited model
- [Reliability] The first PR after the flip is the operational smoke test — if it fails, ROLL BACK the `.claude/dso-config.conf` change first (revert to `model.provider=anthropic`) before debugging, so other open PRs in the repo are not blocked by a misconfigured CI run
- [Hygiene] After the flip, the model IDs in this repo's live config may diverge from the reference config defaults; that's expected and intentional — the reference config is a documented default, the live config is per-repo policy

## Escalation Policy

**Escalation policy**: Proceed unless a significant assumption is required to continue — one that could send the implementation in the wrong direction. Escalate only when genuinely blocked without a reasonable inference. Document all assumptions made without escalating.
data.title: As a project maintainer, I provision an OpenAI API key and configure this project to use OpenAI as the CI review provider
